tools.name: search_global
tools.description: Search objects across spaces. Type keys and option names resolve per space; unresolved spaces produce warnings. Searches loaded spaces using query as full text over names and indexed content. total is a lower bound when clipped; use has_more to request further pages. Warnings report loading or unavailable stores. Each row carries space_id.

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: List spaces. Returns only live spaces accessible to this API key. A space that is deleted, left, or still joining does not appear. has_not_granted_spaces is true when other live user spaces are excluded by the key's grant; if a requested space is missing, ask the user to grant access. This flag is independent of pagination: total and has_more describe only accessible spaces.

ids.description: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id, and the spelling to store outside this API

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a space. A retry the server already handled makes a second space unless it carries the same idempotency key. A dry run validates the body and stops there; creating a space cannot be simulated.

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

ids.description: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id of the new space, and the spelling to store outside this API

tools.name: get_space

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: List chats. Every row carries `unread_messages` and `unread_mentions`, read from the chat state without opening the chat. `include=discussions` adds the space's object discussions: a discussion row's id is the discussion's own id (usable on every chat route) and `parent_id` is the object it belongs to. `unread` keeps only rows with unread messages or unread mentions, and `total` then counts the kept rows.

include.description: discussions adds object discussions to the list; omitted lists chats only

unread.description: messages keeps rows with unread messages; mentions keeps rows with unread mentions

tools.name: create_chat
tools.description: Create a chat. Messages are not blocks. Add them through the messages route; a document edit cannot reach them.

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: get_chat_messages
tools.description: List chat messages. `after` alone walks forward, oldest first, continuing from `next_after`. Every other query is anchored at the newest end and walks backward from `next_before`. Both bounds are exclusive; messages are always ascending. `message_count` is the number of messages the chat holds now; `lifetime_message_count` counts every message ever posted. `offset` is refused.

after.description: Return messages after this order id (exclusive)

before.description: Return messages before this order id (exclusive)

reactions.description: counts (default) returns the emoji counts; full adds the participant ids behind each count

tools.name: add_chat_message
tools.description: Send a chat message. The text is Markdown, formatted as described under Write chat messages. The cap is 8000 UTF-16 code units, where one emoji can cost two or more. Attachments are object ids, at most 32, and each one's kind is taken from the target's layout. In a discussion the text is stored as blocks.

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: edit_chat_message
tools.description: Update chat message text. Every mark is re-derived from the text you send, so a mark the old text carried and the new text does not spell out is lost; in a discussion the text replaces the message's blocks the same way, and dropped quotes or links are named in `warnings`. Attachments and the reply target survive; the style does in a space chat. Editing another member's message is a 403.

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

text.description: The new text, required so an omitted member cannot clear the message by accident; an empty string clears it on purpose.

tools.name: delete_chat_message
tools.description: Delete a chat message. An attachment whose only reference was this message is erased for good afterwards, not moved to Bin. The response names those ids in `warnings`, and a dry run reports the same list without deleting anything. A message that does not exist is a 404 on the dry run too.

dry_run.description: Report what would be deleted, attachments included, without committing

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: toggle_chat_reaction
tools.description: Toggle a chat reaction. `added` says which way the toggle went. A dry run predicts it, but when there is no account identity to predict with it omits the field and says so in `warnings`.

dry_run.description: Report the would-be outcome without committing

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: read_chat
tools.description: Mark chat activity as read. `up_to` is inclusive; it and `last_state_id` come from one messages read: the newest order and the state's id. An empty value would silently mark nothing, so both are required. Later messages stay unread. The reactions scope takes neither field. The receipt carries the chat's state after the move when it could be read back.

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: publish_chat_status
tools.description: Publish chat status. Publishes encrypted ephemeral JSON on status/<chat_id>. Empty text is omitted so clients can show localized typing. data accepts any JSON value. The encoded payload is limited to 65,508 bytes. Status is not stored or replayed; receivers expire it. Success acknowledges acceptance, not delivery.

data.description: optional arbitrary JSON value: object, array, string, number, boolean or null

idempotency_key.description: retry key: send the same value to retry this exact call without applying it twice; one is made for you when omitted

text.description: optional display text; empty or omitted is left out of the pubsub payload so receivers can show a localized typing label; JSON escaping and data consume the same byte budget

match.description: alternative to id: exact text from the block, markdown markup included. Must match exactly one block (repeats in it are fine); several are refused with candidate ids. Give id or match, never both.

recursive.description: default false — deleting a block that has descendants without it is an error naming the descendant count and the resolved block id

op__delete_view.description: Deletes a view from the dataview; the last one is refused. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied. On a type, property ops are written first; a view op refused after that leaves them written.

block.description: a dataview block — optional when the object has exactly one (types, queries and collections do)

view.description: the view to delete (id, full or unique suffix) — deleting the last view is refused; per-view editor state goes with it

op__insert_blocks.description: Inserts new blocks or markdown after, before or inside a block, or at either end of the document. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

after.description: insert after this block's subtree, at its level

before.description: insert before this block, at its level

blocks.description: at most one of after/before/inside targets the run — omit all three to insert at the end of the document (position:first for the start; both work on an empty object); indent 0 = the insertion level

inside.description: insert as children of this block

markdown.description: alternative to blocks; give exactly one. Parsed into flat blocks (headings, lists, checkboxes, fences, quotes, dividers, tables), at most 256. created_blocks keys read ops[i].markdown[j].

position.description: which end to insert at: of the inside container, or of the document itself when no targeting field is given. Refused with after/before. first goes to the start, last appends (the default either way).

op__insert_view.description: Adds a view to the object's dataview, with defaults or copied from another. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied. On a type, property ops are written first; a view op refused after that leaves them written.

after.description: insert after this view (id, full or unique suffix)

block.description: a dataview block — optional when the object has exactly one (types, queries and collections do)

width.description: pixels; null/omitted lets the client pick per format

columns.description: per-column patches keyed by property key: each merges into that property's column (appending one if absent); null removes the column; unnamed columns are untouched — never resend the whole column list

copy_from.description: duplicate this view of the same dataview, everything but its id and name, then apply set and columns on top. Omitted: defaults, every listed property visible, sorted by last_modified_date desc.

name.description: the new view's name (its tab label)

position.description: at most one of after/before/position; omitted = append; the FIRST view is the client's default tab

set.description: merge: only the named fields change, null clears one to its default. sorts and filters replace whole. filter is the compact-string alternative to filters; never both. Columns use the columns channel.

filter.description: compact filter syntax (schema kind filters serves the grammar); parsed server-side into filters

filters.description: filter nodes (schema kind filters), at most 32 at the top level (group more under and/or nodes) — recursive, so prefer filter, the compact string

group_by.description: property key to group by (kanban/board views)

id.description: output-only on reads; accepted back so a read sort round-trips

op__move_block.description: Moves a block and its subtree to a new place. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

id.description: the block to move — its whole subtree moves with it; omit after/before/inside to move it to the end of the document (position:first for the start)

inside.description: moving into the moved block's own subtree is a cycle → error

position.description: which end to move to: of the inside container, or — with NO targeting field — of the document itself, so first moves the block to the start of the document and last to its end (the default either way)

op__move_view.description: Reorders a view among the dataview's views. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied. On a type, property ops are written first; a view op refused after that leaves them written.

block.description: a dataview block — optional when the object has exactly one (types, queries and collections do)

position.description: give exactly one of after/before/position — a destination is required; first makes the view the client's default tab

view.description: the view to move (id, full or unique suffix)

op__remove_items.description: Removes objects from the collection, by id. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

items.description: member object ids to remove from the collection (absent ids are ignored)

op__replace_subtree.description: Replaces one block and its descendants with new blocks. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

blocks.description: replaces the block AND its descendants; indent 0 = the replaced block's level

op__replace_text.description: Replaces text inside one block, markup preserved. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

find.description: exact text within one block, markup included. Must match once in that block unless replace_all. A match touching markup metadata (a link destination) is rejected. Without id it must find one block.

id.description: optional — omit it and find locates the block: the find text must appear in exactly ONE block, or the op refuses (several matching blocks → the error lists candidate ids to retry with)

replace.description: literal replacement, applied in the parsed text-and-marks model: markup bytes cannot create or remove marks. An empty string deletes the match. The result may not exceed 1048576 UTF-16 units.

replace_all.description: default false — replaces every occurrence WITHIN the one matched block; it never widens the locator to several blocks

op__set_cell.description: Sets one table cell, by row and column. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

col.description: column id (full or unique suffix), or the column's header text (served as header on each column in the read) — case-insensitive, must name exactly one column

row.description: row id (full or unique suffix), or the row's first-cell text — case-insensitive, must name exactly one row

value.description: string = paragraph shorthand, null = clear, or a block object / array of blocks

op__set_properties.description: Sets, adds to, removes from or unsets property values on the object. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

add.description: list-shaped keys only (select, multi_select, objects, files): append entries without rewriting the array — existing entries are never duplicated; unknown option NAMES are created

remove.description: list-shaped keys only: delete matching entries — absent entries (and absent keys) are a no-op; a key may appear in only one of set/unset/add/remove

set.description: property key → value (a list-shaped key takes an array of option names or ids); presence is meaningful — an empty array means present-but-empty; unknown select option names are created

op__set_type.description: Changes the object's type and converts the document to the new type's layout. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

type.description: the type the object becomes, by key, api key or name. Only layouts of one family convert (basic, todo, note, profile and bookmark among themselves; otherwise the same layout), and a refused change names the types this object can take. The document is rewritten for the new layout: to note the name becomes the first block, from note the first block becomes the name

op__update_block.description: Changes fields of one existing block, found by id or by its text. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied.

id.description: the block to update — give this or match, never both

match.description: alternative to id: exact text from the block, markdown markup included. Must match exactly one block (repeats in it are fine); several are refused with candidate ids. Give id or match, never both.

set.description: merge semantics: only the named fields change — text included only if named; null clears a field; id and indent are rejected (use move_block to re-nest)

op__update_view.description: Changes a view's fields or columns on the object's dataview. One entry of {"ops":[…]}, the request body (example_body shows it wrapped); 1 to 512 entries apply in order as one edit — if any one is refused, none is applied. On a type, property ops are written first; a view op refused after that leaves them written.

block.description: a dataview block — optional when the object has exactly one (types, queries and collections do)

width.description: pixels; null/omitted lets the client pick per format

columns.description: per-column patches keyed by property key: each merges into that property's column (appending one if absent); null removes the column; unnamed columns are untouched — never resend the whole column list

set.description: merge: only the named fields change, null clears one to its default. sorts and filters replace whole. filter is the compact-string alternative to filters; never both. Columns use the columns channel.

filter.description: compact filter syntax (schema kind filters serves the grammar); parsed server-side into filters

filters.description: filter nodes (schema kind filters), at most 32 at the top level (group more under and/or nodes) — recursive, so prefer filter, the compact string

group_by.description: property key to group by (kanban/board views)

id.description: output-only on reads; accepted back so a read sort round-trips

view.description: view id, full or unique suffix — optional when the dataview has exactly one view

System objects are a 403 as well. A dry run reports the verdict without the checks that run at archive time, so a deletable verdict can still meet a 403.

Chats, types, templates and system objects cannot hold one.

rows.description: Table rows. The implicit cell-id grid is rows × columns and must not exceed 100,000 pairs, including empty cells.

blockAlign.description: Horizontal alignment by name, shared by a block's `align`, a view column's `align` and the `layout_align` property value. An unknown name is rejected; only the property value also takes a raw number.

text.description:

  `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strikethrough~~`, `` `code` ``

  `[text](anytype://object?objectId=<id>)` links to an object in this space
  `[text](anytype://object?objectId=<id>&spaceId=<space_id>)` links to an object in another space
  `<mention object_id="<id>">text</mention>` is a decorated object reference
  `<u>underline</u>`, `<font color="red">text</font>`, `<font background="yellow">text</font>`

url.description: Input alias for `text`, accepted only on a service `processor`. Stating both is refused. A renderer processor, or an absent `processor`, refuses this member. Export always writes `text`.

added_at.description: When the file was added, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Export writes full UTC (`2026-07-06T15:04:05Z`); input also takes an offset, fractional seconds or a bare date. A date no calendar has is refused.

object_id.description: The block's target object as a reference: the whole string is the id. See $defs/objectRef. A reference carries no caption or name after it, so nothing here is split.

fields.description: A `row` and a `column` carry no attributes of their own; their children are the content. The one exception lives in the output-only bag: a layout column's width.

width.description: A layout column's share of its row, as a fraction from 0 to just over 1, where 0 means unset. A table column's `width` is a first-class property in pixels instead.

property.description: The property this block renders inline, by its document-facing spelling (`Due date`). Every slot spelled `property` names one that way.

is_collection.description: Selects a curated list when `object_id` is absent or empty. If true, read this document's `collection_items`. Else a non-empty legacy `source`, then a type document's own objects, else `query_source`.

object_id.description: The object this view takes its records from: a query, collection or type document, or this one. When authoring, set it only on a non-query, non-collection host. Empty means absent.

source.description: Legacy source of a detached inline query, read only when `object_id` is absent or empty, `is_collection` is not true and it is non-empty. Entries travel verbatim. Output only.

limit.description: How many entries the widget shows, 0 to int32 max. The whole range is allowed here, because this block is the fallback for a widget above the flat index cap at $defs/widgetListingLimit.

fields.description: Verbatim internal per-block data, minus keys lifted into first-class properties (`lang` to `language`). Output only. A link's `cardStyle`, `iconSize`, `description` and `relations` are stale copies.

cardStyle.description: How a link renders: a plain text row (the default), a card, or inline. Shared by the link block and a bundle index's widgets.

source.description: Where this image came from. Export writes it; an author omits it, since an uploaded image has no provenance to claim.

cover.description: The object's cover: one of three kinds, chosen by `format`. The flat coverId, coverType, coverScale, coverX and coverY keys are refused in `properties`.

format.description: Which kind of cover this is: an image object in this space, a flat colour, or a gradient.

dataviewProperty.description: One entry of a dataview's `properties[]`: a property available to the block's views, with its format. A column, sort or filter may name a property this list does not carry.

property.description: The property this entry declares, by its document-facing spelling (`Due date`). The view's `columns[]`, `sorts[]` and `filters[]` refer to it by that same spelling.

file.description: The image, as the id of a file object in this bundle. A raw content cid travels in the `cid` variant instead.

cid.description: The image's raw content cid (dag-pb or raw codec, normally starting `bafybei`), fetched from content storage. Never an object reference. Output only: an author supplies an image as a file object.

emoji.description: A legacy emoji superseded by this named icon, carried so export loses nothing. Export writes it; supplying it does not choose the icon, since `format` already did.

icon.description: The object's icon: one of five kinds, chosen by `format`. The flat iconEmoji, iconImage, iconName and iconOption keys are refused in `properties`.

allOf.description: Which kind of icon this is: an emoji, an image object in this space, an image by raw content cid (no object behind it), a built-in named icon, or a bare colour.
Which kind of icon this is: an emoji, an image object in this space, an image by raw content cid (no object behind it), a built-in named icon, or a bare colour.

iconColor.description: One of the ten palette colours, the same palette select options use, or a raw number, 1 to 9007199254740991, for a stored value the palette has no name for.

iconSize.description: The icon size on a link's card. Defaults to none.

cid.description: The image's raw content cid (dag-pb or raw codec, normally starting `bafybei`), fetched from content storage. Never an object reference. Output only: an author supplies an image as a file object.

emoji.description: A legacy emoji superseded by this named icon, carried so export loses nothing. Export writes it; supplying it does not choose the icon, since `format` already did.

iconVariants.description: The icon variant rules shared by every icon slot. It carries the per-variant conditions but not the set of variant names: each slot states its own.

format.description: Which kind of icon this is: an emoji, an image object in this space, an image by raw content cid (no object behind it), a built-in named icon, or a bare colour.

imageKind.description: What an image was uploaded for, by name: the vocabulary of the `image_kind` property value, set on file objects.

importType.description: Which importer created an import- or usecase-originated object, by name: the vocabulary of the `import_type` property value. A name outside this set is refused.

linkDescription.description: What the link's card shows under the title: nothing (the default), the manually written description, or the target's own content.

objectLayout.description: The closed set of object layouts, by name. A name outside this set is refused; a raw number is accepted beside a name, so a stored value outside the vocabulary round-trips as its number.

objectOrigin.description: How an object entered its space, by name: the vocabulary of the `origin` property value. An unknown name is refused, and so is a number this set can name; only an unnamed number passes.

objectRef.description: The id of an object in this space or a bundle-local slug, whole: nothing appended, nothing split. An object id is dag-cbor (`bafyrei`); a content cid (`bafybei`) is not one. Never a URL or file path.

opaqueName.description: A name from a vocabulary this format does not enumerate: the app's icon, cover-colour and gradient sets. Only the shape is checked; an unknown name shows as no icon.

participantPermissions.description: What a space member may do, by name: the vocabulary of the `participant_permissions` property value. These are the stored identifiers, not the API's viewer, editor and admin roles.

participantStatus.description: Where a space member is in joining or leaving the space, by name: the vocabulary of the `participant_status` property value.

file.description: The image, as the id of a file object in this bundle. A raw content cid travels in the `cid` variant instead.

cid.description: The image's raw content cid (dag-pb or raw codec, normally starting `bafybei`), fetched from content storage. Never an object reference. Output only: an author supplies an image as a file object.

emoji.description: A legacy emoji superseded by this named icon, carried so export loses nothing. Export writes it; supplying it does not choose the icon, since `format` already did.

plainIcon.description: An icon restricted to what a callout block and a bundle index can hold: an emoji, or an image as a file object in this space or the raw `cid` variant export writes.

allOf.description: Which kind of icon this is: an emoji, an image object in this space, an image by raw content cid (no object behind it), a built-in named icon, or a bare colour.

propertyDefinition.description: One property, in the one shape this format uses wherever it describes a property. `property` is the document-facing spelling, `internal_key` the stored id; each home adds its own requirements.

internal_key.description: The property's stored internal key: a bson id for a custom property (`6a83296f61fab2265263ae34`) or the camelCase key of a bundled one (`dueDate`). An author omits it; a spelling resolves or mints it.

object_types.description: objects and files only: the types the property may point at, in priority order, each as the derived id `type-<internal_key>`. A display name or the legacy `ot-<key>` is accepted on input.

property.description: The property's document-facing spelling, such as `Due date`. A spelling, never a stored id; the stored id is `internal_key`.

propertyFormat.description: A property format by name: the public API vocabulary plus the internal formats a store carries (emoji, objects, properties, map). An authorable slot may not state `map`.

propertyMap.description: The object's property values, keyed by spelling. On a list format a bare value and a one-element array are the same value; on a single-valued format an array is not unwrapped.

querySource.description: For a query object, what the query ranges over. A type target matches every object of that type, a property target every object carrying it; targets combine with `or`. `{}` is a query with no target.

properties.description: Property targets: every object carrying the property matches, whatever its value. Each is the property's stored internal key, bare (`lastModifiedDate`, `6a83296f61fab2265263ae34`).

types.description: Type targets: every object of the type matches. Each is the type's derived id `type-<internal_key>`, the id that type's own document carries. A display name or legacy `ot-<key>` is read on input.

header.description: The header row's cell text for this column, linking the header word to the column id a table edit addresses. Written only by an API read that asks for it; ignored on input.

name.description: When `name` supplies the property identity, it is NFC-normalized before the 128-character key bound applies. This schema checks the non-empty, control-free part; readers enforce the bound.

typeProperty.description: One entry of a type document's property list: a property definition plus `uninstalled` and `section`. Identify the property with `property`, `internal_key`, or a `name` to derive the spelling from.

internal_key.description: The property's stored internal key: a bson id for a custom property (`6a83296f61fab2265263ae34`) or the camelCase key of a bundled one (`dueDate`). An author omits it; a spelling resolves or mints it.

allOf.description: objects and files only: the types the property may point at, in priority order, each as the derived id `type-<internal_key>`. A display name or the legacy `ot-<key>` is accepted on input.

property.description: The property's document-facing spelling, such as `Due date`. A spelling, never a stored id; the stored id is `internal_key`.

uninstalled.description: The user removed this property from the space. The object stays and is hidden. Export writes `true` only; absent means the same as `false`. An author never writes it, and a reader never installs it.

viewColumn.description: One column of a view: which property it shows, plus display facts (width, alignment, an aggregation). Column order is display order.

property.description: The property this column shows, by its document-facing spelling. The sorts, filters and the dataview's `properties[]` entries use that same spelling.

viewType.description: How a dataview view renders. Shared by a view's own `type` and a type's `default_view`, so the two cannot drift apart.

api_key.description: The option's public API key, the spelling callers address it by. Not a slug of the name: it does not follow a rename. Export writes it where the store holds one; an author never writes one.

internal_key.description: The option's stored key, a minted id. An author never writes one, and export writes it only where it exists.

widgetLayout.description: How a sidebar widget renders: `link` is a single row (the default), `tree` expands children, `list` and `compact_list` show contents, `view` renders a type's or query's own view.

widgetListingLimit.description: How many entries a sidebar listing widget shows: the product cap for a bundle index's flat widget. The widget block's own `limit` takes the whole int32 range instead.
